automatic_gains.description:
This feature adjusts the control parameters of your heating system dynamically, optimizing temperature control for better comfort and energy efficiency. Enabling this option allows SAT to continuously adapt and fine-tune the heating settings based on the environmental conditions. This helps maintain a stable and comfortable environment without manual intervention.

Note: If you choose not to enable automatic gains, you will need to manually enter the PID values for precise temperature control. Please ensure that you have accurate PID values for your specific heating system to achieve optimal performance.
automatic_gains.title: Automatic Gains

manufacturer.description: We have attempted to identify the most suitable manufacturer for your heating system based on your gateway type and device information. However, if this does not match your setup, you can select a different manufacturer from the list.

data_description.climate_valve_offset: Temperature gap (target vs current) required to treat a valve as open.
data_description.flame_off_setpoint_offset_celsius: When the flame is off, hold a temporary setpoint at the selected source temperature + offset (Pulse Width Modulation only).
data_description.maximum_consumption: Gas use at maximum modulation, used for consumption estimation.
data_description.maximum_relative_modulation: Cap the boiler modulation percentage (0–100) to limit maximum output.
data_description.minimum_consumption: Gas use at minimum modulation, used for consumption estimation.
data_description.modulation_suppression_delay_seconds: Time after flame-on before suppression can apply (Pulse Width Modulation only).
data_description.modulation_suppression_offset_celsius: How much to lower the flow setpoint during suppression (Pulse Width Modulation only).
data_description.flow_setpoint_offset_celsius: Minimum offset below boiler temperature when clamping setpoint (continuous mode).
data_description.minimum_boiler_pressure: Lower pressure threshold for health detection (bar).
data_description.maximum_boiler_pressure: Upper pressure threshold for health detection (bar).
data_description.maximum_pressure_drop_rate: Maximum allowed pressure drop rate before flagging health (bar/h).
data_description.pressure_max_value_age: Maximum age of a pressure reading before marking health as unhealthy.
data_description.solar_gain_compensation: Reduce requested heat when indoor temperature rises quickly from likely sunlight.
data_description.solar_gain_freeze_integral: Avoid integral wind-up while solar gain compensation is active.
data_description.solar_gain_min_elevation: Minimum sun elevation (degrees) required before solar gain detection can trigger.
data_description.solar_gain_min_rise_per_hour: Minimum indoor temperature rise rate required to detect solar gain (°C/h).
data_description.solar_gain_setpoint_offset_celsius: Temporary requested setpoint reduction applied while solar gain is active.
data_description.target_temperature_step: Step size for target temperature adjustments in the UI.
data_description.thermal_comfort: Enable the use of the Simmer Index for thermal comfort adjustment.
data_description.simulation: Enable simulation mode (no real boiler commands are sent).
data_description.error_monitoring: Send SAT-related errors to the developer via Sentry to help diagnose issues.
data_description.force_pulse_width_modulation: Force Pulse Width Modulation even when modulation control is available (useful for relay-style control).
data_description.flame_off_setpoint_source: Base for the temporary setpoint while the Pulse Width Modulation ON phase waits for the flame. Choose the flow temperature if your boiler does not report a return temperature.

data_description.derivative: The derivative term (kD) in the PID controller, responsible for mitigating overshooting.
data_description.heating_curve_coefficient: The coefficient used to adjust the heating curve.
data_description.integral: The integral term (kI) in the PID controller, responsible for reducing steady-state error.
data_description.maximum_setpoint: The optimal temperature for efficient boiler operation.
data_description.proportional: The proportional term (kP) in the PID controller, responsible for the immediate response to errors.
data_description.window_sensors: Contact Sensors that trigger the system to react when a window or door is open for a period of time.

room_presets.title: Room Presets
room_presets.description: Pick the room to set preset temperatures for. The home temperature is the room's normal target and defaults to the house home temperature. Presets you do not tick only lower the room relative to it and never raise it.

room_preset.title: Room Presets
room_preset.description: What each preset means for {room}. Tick the presets this room has its own temperature for.

data_description.fixed: Presets never change the target temperature of this room.
data_description.own: Only the ticked presets use the temperature set below; the others follow the house preset.

reset_integral.name: Reset Integral
reset_integral.description: This service resets the integrating part of the PID controller for the specified climate entity. This may be useful if the integral value has become too large or if the PID controller's performance has degraded.

pulse_width_modulation.name: Pulse Width Modulation
pulse_width_modulation.description: Force enable or disable the Pulse Width Modulation, do note that it may be turned on or off automatically right after again.

enabled.name: Enabled
enabled.description: The state you want to force.

boiler_fault.title: Boiler reports a fault
boiler_fault.description: The boiler connected to {name} reports a fault (code {fault_code}). Check the boiler display and consult the manual or your installer.

boiler_pressure.title: Boiler pressure unhealthy
boiler_pressure.description: The boiler pressure for {name} is out of range or dropping fast (currently {pressure} bar). Check the system for leaks and top up the water pressure if needed.

boiler_pressure_trend.title: Boiler slowly losing pressure
boiler_pressure_trend.description: The heating system for {name} has lost about {loss} bar since its last top-up and was topped up {top_ups} times in the last 90 days. This can point to a slow leak or a failing expansion vessel. Check the system or contact your installer.

boiler_short_cycling_trend.title: Boiler short cycling more often
boiler_short_cycling_trend.description: The boiler for {name} now starts about {recent_cycles} times a day with a median run time of {on_time} minutes, compared with {baseline_cycles} starts a day in similar weather. Frequent short runs wear the boiler and waste gas. Check the heating curve, the PWM settings and the boiler's minimum output.

room_undersupplied.title: {room} receives too little heat
room_undersupplied.description: {room} on {name} consistently needs more heat than the rest of the house, which raises the flow temperature by about {flow_premium} °C. Check whether the radiator is large enough, whether the lockshield valves are balanced, and whether there are drafts or open doors.

room_sensor_mismatch.title: {room} stays cold while its thermostat is satisfied
room_sensor_mismatch.description: {room} on {name} stays below its target, but its thermostat rarely asks for heat. The thermostat probably reads warmer than the room. Check its placement or temperature offset.

room_fault.title: {room} reports a valve problem
room_fault.description: The device in {room} on {name} reports a valve alarm. Check its installation, calibration and any external temperature sensor link.
